clauses.title: How to File a Complaint
clauses.text:
How consumers can file complaints about substandard or counterfeit ISI-marked products:
1. BIS Care App: Available on Android (Google Play) and iOS (App Store). Scan the ISI mark or enter the license number to report a complaint directly.
2. BIS Website: Online complaint form at www.bis.gov.in → 'Consumer Corner' → 'File a Complaint'.
3. Email: Send complaint details to ccd@bis.gov.in (Consumer Complaints Division).
4. Toll-free Helpline: 1800-11-4100 (available Monday–Friday, 9:30 AM to 5:30 PM IST).
5. Written Complaint: Send by post to the nearest BIS Regional/Branch Office.

Required information for complaints: Product details, ISI mark number, CM/L number, date of purchase, seller details, nature of complaint, and photographic evidence if possible.

clauses.title: How to Verify ISI Mark Authenticity
clauses.text:
How to verify if an ISI mark is genuine:
A genuine ISI mark consists of:
1. The ISI logo (a triangular figure with 'ISI' text inside)
2. The IS standard number (e.g., IS 2347 for pressure cookers)
3. A CM/L (Certification Marks License) number unique to the manufacturer

Verification methods:
1. BIS Care App: Enter the CM/L number to verify the manufacturer's license status.
2. BIS Website: Visit www.bis.gov.in → 'Know Your Standards' → 'Verify License'.
3. Check the CM/L number format: It follows the pattern 'CM/L-XXXXXXX' where X are digits.

Warning signs of fake ISI marks:
- Blurry or poorly printed ISI logo
- Missing CM/L number
- CM/L number that returns 'no record found' on BIS portal
- ISI mark without the IS standard number
- Products from categories where ISI mark is mandatory but mark looks suspicious

clauses.title: Penalties for Misuse of ISI Mark and BIS Standards
clauses.text:
Penalties under BIS Act 2016 for misuse:
1. Using ISI mark without license: Fine of ₹2 lakh to ₹5 lakh, imprisonment up to 2 years, or both.
2. Using counterfeit ISI mark: Fine up to ₹10 lakh and imprisonment up to 2 years.
3. Selling non-conforming products with ISI mark: Fine of minimum ₹1 lakh or 10 times the value of goods (whichever is more).
4. Selling without mandatory BIS certification (for compulsory items): Fine of ₹2 lakh + ₹2 lakh for each subsequent offence.
5. Obstructing BIS officers during inspection: Fine up to ₹1 lakh.

BIS has the power to:
- Suspend or cancel licenses
- Order product recall
- File criminal complaints
- Seize non-conforming goods
- Publish names of non-compliant manufacturers

clauses.title: BIS Standards Clubs for Students
clauses.text:
BIS Standards Club Scheme:
- Purpose: Promote quality awareness among students through Standards Clubs in schools, colleges, and polytechnics.
- Eligibility: Any recognized educational institution can establish a Standards Club.
- Activities: Workshops on standardization, visits to BIS offices and labs, poster/essay competitions, quality awareness campaigns.
- Benefits: Students gain awareness about BIS certification, ISI mark, hallmarking, and quality consciousness.
- Registration: Apply through the nearest BIS Branch Office or online at www.bis.gov.in.
- BIS provides resource materials and guest speakers for Standards Club events.
